profile.headline: Software Engineer at Splunk
profile.summary:
My background provides perspectives from technical, business, and client-oriented standpoints. I have a strong interest in roles that both require and give me exposure to a diverse skillset and team to reflect my passions and abilities. 

-- 
Looking to explore: Software Engineering, Product Management, Data Analytics, Innovation, Consulting,  & Business Analytics.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
• Developed and operationalized cloud-native RESTful Microservices APIs to provide admins programmatic management capabilities and assisted in transitioning customers to Splunk Cloud. In production. 
• Worked in projects leveraging CI/CD pipeline, Kubernetes, Docker, Go

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
• Teaching Assistant for Introduction to Computer Systems Course where topics taught include: UNIX, Command Line, C programming, Dynamic Memory Management, and Process Control
• Lead office hours and review course material with students 
• Debug, assist students with, and grade course projects

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Developed full stack, production level code for En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) Web Applications in Spring and Flask
• Reduced initial load time of data grid of 10000+ deliverables from 15s. to 1s. by creating new dynamic load/server-side processing capabilities in open-source code

company.name: Advanced Cybersecurity Experience for Students (ACES) Honors Program

positions.title: President
positions.description:
• Presided over weekly meetings between student leaders and ACES Staff
• Empowered student body by mediating town halls and voicing student feedback to ACES staff 
• Organized academic and social events for ACES Student Body 
• Negotiated with vendors and suppliers for social events

positions.title: Client Consultant - Technical Lead
positions.description:
• Investigated causes of inefficiencies in the Electrical and Computer Engineering advising processes by analyzing current flow of data and student/advisor communication 
• Developed Google Apps Script, HTML response email, and Google Sheet template to automate manual data processing and filtering completed by staff (script is currently used by University of Maryland's ECE Advising Department) 
• Streamlined the process by eliminating the need for multiple applications (WuFoo, Excel, Yet
Another Mail Merge) and instead creating a fully GSuite solution 
• Minimized time spent on registration paperwork, complexities, delays, and student misconceptions in the registration process

company.name: University of Maryland - A. James Clark School of Engineering

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
• Teaching Assistant for Foundations of Cybersecurity course at the University of Maryland
• Topics taught include UNIX, Bash Scripting, Command Line, and Networking concepts
• Assisted Professor with lessons and content demonstration during lecture

positions.title: Summer Ambassador
positions.description:
• Developed and taught curriculum in Python, HTML5/CSS/JavaScript, and Computing Principles to over 100 K-12 students at the Iribe Initiative computer science camps.
• Fostered a supportive and collaborative environment to inspire and empower kids from underrepresented groups in the field to pursue computer science

positions.title: Programming Intern
positions.description:
• Designed project proposal to utilize Google Apps scripting to streamline volunteer outreach and scheduling processes through automated texts and email reminders
• Volunteered for tabling and outreach initiatives and assist in lobbying elected officials in Annapolis and Capitol Hill

educations.schoolName: University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business

honors.description: Recipient of University of Maryland's most prestigious scholarship. The Banneker/Key award is a full, 4-Year Merit Scholarship to the University of Maryland and awarded to the top 1% of accepted students.
